title: AI Operations
intro: We run Hello Robo as an AI-native studio, and this role is how we keep it that way. You'll find every manual step in how we run creative projects, hand it to AI agents, and keep the work moving while you do it.

Our designers should spend their time designing, and clients should always know what happens next. Because our timelines live inside our clients' build cycles, you also need to understand how robots actually get built.
workOn: Process mapping → Map how projects move through the studio, from first lead to final delivery, and find where the hours leak out.
AI agents → Build and run agents for the repetitive work: call notes and recaps, status updates, briefs, asset tracking, invoice reminders, and reporting.
Connected tools → Wire up Notion, Slack, Figma, Gmail, and Webflow so information moves between them without anyone copying it by hand.
Redundancy hunting → If the team does something twice, it should happen once, or on its own.
Measured gains → Track the hours each agent saves and keep a running log of what works, what broke, and what to build next.
Team enablement → Document every flow you build and teach the team to use it, so the automation sticks.
Project coordination → Run Monday kickoffs and client calls, send recaps within hours, and keep deadlines and risks visible.
Robotics timelines → Line up our design milestones with the client's build cycle — prototypes, testing, pilots, trade shows, funding rounds, and deployments — so the work lands when it matters.
Studio admin & leads → Keep contracts, NDAs, invoices, and lead follow-ups on track, run by agents wherever they can be.
bring: You're AI-native. Agents are how you already work every day, not something you're planning to try.
Real examples of studio or agency operations you've automated with AI agents — kickoffs, recaps, asset chasing, invoicing, lead follow-ups. Show us what you built and how many hours it saved.
Hands-on with Claude, ChatGPT, Zapier, Make, n8n, or Notion AI. Comfortable with prompts, APIs, MCP, and simple scripts.
Good judgment about which steps an agent should own and which need a human.
A working understanding of how robotics companies build products: hardware and software development cycles, prototyping, testing, pilots, and deployment. This is a must.
1–3 years in project coordination, operations, or a similar role — agency experience preferred.
Obsessively organized. You follow up without being asked.
Calm, clear presence on client calls and excellent written English.
Based in New York City and able to work from our studio.
niceToHave: Experience building custom agents, GPTs, or Claude projects for a team.
Experience at a design studio, or at a robotics or hardware startup.
howWeWork: Twice-weekly Slack updates keep pulses steady.
Small team, flat hierarchy, big ownership.
We meet once a year in different parts of the world to connect, plan, and reset.
applySteps: Links or short walkthroughs of studio operations you've automated with AI agents, and the time each one saved.
The first process you'd hand to an agent at a design studio (tweet length).
outro: If every repetitive task looks to you like a job for an agent, we'd love to meet you.
